chapter: Rising in Manhattan: clubs, Hilda and the Latin scene
title: Writing "Sopa de Pichon"
summary: He improvised the tune at the Park Plaza over a vamp from Frank Ayala, naming neighborhood tough guys in the lyrics.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I see. Okay. Macho, I understand there - that's where you wrote "Sopa de Pichon", your first hit and "La Paella" and a lot of other things for the years to come, that you lived there. What inspired your first hit recording, "Sopa de Pichon"?
Oh!! "Sopa de Pichon" - because, you know, there was ahh an atmosphere, happy atmosphere, and about - have a good time, forget it - and they called that particular happy cigarette. "Pichon"........

........sopa, pito, you name it, so, I don't know how come to my mind to write something about that, because I wasn't a - I never composed in my life. Never wrote anything. So that particular tune, we played for Perez at the Park Plaza. we had no arrangement, we don't have anything. I said to Frank Ayala 'okay get a vamp in D' so he start: bam barambam bam bi - 'tiene que tomarte una sopa de pichon' and then start to improvise lyrics, like calypso like........

......and I used to mention in my inspiration all the tough guys of the neighborhood so that what became a hit in that particular place. Naturally, in the recording there was a different lyrics, but at that particular place, I used to use Emilio Guardia, Cabo Carola, all those tough guys in the neighborhood and then .....
